description:
Store each gate run at `gate-runs/<issue-id>/<run-id>.json`, so an issue's run history is one directory and no reader enumerates other issues' runs.

## Background

`VirtualPath::gate_run_record(&GateRunId)` and `VirtualPath::gate_run_directory(&GateRunId)` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/path.rs`, with the constant `GATE_RUN_RECORD_FILE`) build the flat `gate-runs/<run-id>/result.json`, and `path.rs` holds their own test.

Callers: the finalizer's gate-run pass and the new-run capture `gate_run_record_paths` (`commands/mod.rs`), which takes no issue although its callers have it; `validation/record_fidelity.rs`; `validation/repository.rs` (`:1068`, `:1096`, and `:1036`, a test helper that reads the first root entry as a run id); `crates/server/src/watcher.rs:324`; `storage/issue_store_conformance.rs`; `storage/reference.rs`; `gate_execution.rs`.

The finalizer creates each run's directory with `ExpectedPreimage::Absent`, which fails on an issue's second run under the new layout.

Two enumerators have no issue until they parse a record: `record_drift` (`validation/record_fidelity.rs`) and `discover_gate_run_results` (`commands/mod.rs`), both reached from `capture_record_fidelity_validation` (`commands/validate.rs`). `captured_gate_run_ids` (`repository_state/mutation.rs`) filters on run directories. That capture uses `MUTATION_CAPTURE_BUDGET`, whose 256 listings (enforced in `CaptureSpec::validate`) cannot hold one listing per issue.

Fixtures spelling the layout: `storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs` and `storage/issue_store_conformance.rs` (`gate_run_directory`, `GATE_RUN_RECORD_FILE`). Existence checks in `tests/cli_gate/` go through the constructor and need no change; the server watcher matches any path component and needs only its test call updated.

The generated reference explains that the layout is flat "rather than nested per issue" (`storage/reference.rs`, rendered into `docs/reference/storage-records.md`), and the `GateRunResult` rustdoc names `gate-runs/<run-id>/result.json` (`domain/types.rs`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `VirtualPath::gate_run_record(&IssueId, &GateRunId)` names `gate-runs/<issue-id>/<run-id>.json`, its own test pins that path, and every caller passes the run's issue. `gate_run_directory(&GateRunId)` and `GATE_RUN_RECORD_FILE` no longer exist; `gate_run_issue_directory(&IssueId)` names an issue's directory.
- [hard] REQ-02: The shared reader lists one issue's runs by reading `gate-runs/<issue-id>/` only and parses only its records. The conformance case shows that a corrupt record of another issue fails no lookup and applies its clutter rules inside the issue's directory.
- [hard] REQ-03: `gate_run_record_paths` takes the issue and requests the root, the issue's directory and each record. The finalizer creates the issue's directory only when its captured entry is absent, and a test records two runs on one issue and runs on two issues.
- [hard] REQ-04: `capture_record_fidelity_validation` uses a dedicated budget of 65,536 listings with the existing byte limit, and `discover_gate_run_results` enumerates `gate-runs/` by one listing per issue directory, skipping `verdicts/`. `captured_gate_run_ids` yields `(IssueId, GateRunId)` pairs, and `record_drift` reports a record whose `issue_id` differs from its directory.
- [hard] REQ-05: No file under `crates/` spells `result.json` or `gate-runs/<run>` for a run record. Every test that plants or names a record builds its path through the constructor, including the helper in `validation/repository.rs`.
- [hard] REQ-06: The reference source and the `GateRunResult` rustdoc describe `gate-runs/<issue-id>/<run-id>.json` and the per-issue history listing, with no flat-layout rationale, and the committed reference is regenerated by `scripts/generate-storage-records-reference.sh` and matches the projection.

## Notes

- Manual gate attestations already publish gate-run records carrying their attestor, time and status. They move with every other run, and the latest-run and history views still show each attestation.
- The dedicated budget keeps the byte limit as the guard against growth; the listing bound scales with issues, and only whole-repository validation pays it.
title: Gate-run records live under their issue
